sections.strategy: No new F&F announcements surfaced for 21–28 September; the brand is still bedding in its revamped F&F Online experience (refreshed web/app design, curated styling inspiration, a new Wishlist and better search), with Tesco saying more launches, sizes and online-exclusive ranges are coming. It builds on F&F clothing sales rising 5.1% to over £1.2bn in FY25/26, led by womenswear, activewear and the curated F&F Edit.
sections.pricing: No F&F-specific price changes this week. The value-tier backdrop remains competitive: Primark's recent 'Iconic Value' cuts of up to 29% keep pressure on entry prices, while Sainsbury's Tu is moving upmarket with its 'most elevated' AW26 collection (4x the premium knitwear options, including cashmere, mohair and alpaca). F&F continues to lean on Clubcard-exclusive pricing to stand out.
sections.launches: No new F&F drops were confirmed this week. The latest activity remains the 400 new online styles launched on 17 September (funnel-neck track jackets, co-ords, leopard-print skirts) and the AW26 pop-up at Frameless Gallery, Marble Arch, on 18 September during London Fashion Week.
soWhat: F&F's online assortment is still growing, with more sizes and online-exclusive ranges promised. That favours suppliers who can run small, fast-turn style drops and extended size runs, rather than only large replenishment volumes.

The value tier is splitting: Primark is cutting prices while Tu adds premium fibres. Expect F&F buyers to push hard on cost for core lines while testing higher-spec knitwear and outerwear, so get quotes ready for both.

With no F&F sourcing or sustainability news this week, check Tesco's 2026 Sustainability Report (six new or updated commitments, including circularity and supply-chain decarbonisation) for clothing-specific requirements ahead of AW27/SS27 vendor reviews.
